title: Hue Citadel (Capital City and Inner City), Vietnam
summary: The Nguyen dynasty's walled capital at Hue, Vietnam, planned in 1803-1805 and completed in 1832, after Hue became capital of unified Viet Nam in 1802. Its outer Capital City is a square of 2,235 m a side inside walls 6.6 m high; it was damaged in 1885, 1947 and 1968.

uncertainty.note: ICOMOS: planning from 1803 to 1805, construction complete in 1832. UNESCO: capital of unified Viet Nam established in 1802.

as_recorded.value: not until 1832 that construction was complete

reviewer_note: Shape wall (square enceinte, side 2,235 m, height 6.6 m); the ICOMOS PDF is OCR and prints 'm' as 'rn', which I read as metres. The 'originally 6.6 m' height is the Capital City wall as built. Pin is OSM's Hoang Thanh (Imperial City) node inside the Inner City, within 1 km of the enclosure's centre but I did not open a coordinate for the citadel centre. 'Intact 1832-1885' bridges an undated period.
